data.label: panic-1440-panic-from-song-channel
data.caption: From Song, hold the Channel button (3,8) for about two seconds, then release it. Panic sends Note Off to the connected MIDI outputs to release stuck notes. This example starts silent, so you hear no change and the screen stays on Song. Panic leaves playback running. Holding the button of the page you are already on does nothing.

Skip to controls
MOSAIC

1.4.0 / QUICK REFERENCE

Interactive manual
Switch light / dark

Find a control here, then follow its heading for setup and full steps.

Find a control
Clear
130 of 130 features
Getting Started

Install Mosaic and configure one channel before creating a song.

Installing Mosaic

Install Mosaic from maiden or the norns community catalogue.

Configuring an Output

Route channel 1 to one instrument.

Hardware Requirements

Mosaic requires norns and a 128 grid.

MIDI Device Configuration

Device configurations define output defaults and mapped parameters.

Installing Stock Device Configurations

Copy selected stock JSON files into data/mosaic/config.

Creating a Custom Device Configuration

Create a JSON map from the instrument’s MIDI implementation.

Lock lead time

Set the lead time for MIDI parameter locks before their step.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
PARAMS → MOSAIC → Parameter locks → Lock lead time (ms)	Set the global MIDI lock lead from 0 to 50 ms (default 25).
Selecting an n.b. Player

Install and enable a supported player before assigning it to a channel.

MIDI Keyboard Input

Hold a step to enter it, or arm recording and play.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Select channel; Record off; no step held; play MIDI keys	Audition the selected channel’s output without entering step masks.
Select channel → hold step → play MIDI keys	Enter that step’s note, velocity and chord masks.
Record (2,8) + running transport + MIDI keys	Record onto the selected channel’s active steps.
MIDI Controller Mapping

Assign MIDI controls to channel parameters through the norns MIDI Map menu.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Native PARAMS: hold K1 and press K3	Switch between EDIT and MAP modes.
Map editor: select Learn and press K3; operate MIDI control	Learn its CC, input channel and device.
Map editor: press K2	Leave the editor and save the assignment.
Operate assigned relative MIDI control	Change the mapped Mosaic value.
Controls and Navigation

Use the bottom-row page keys and check the screen header.

Starting and Stopping Playback

Grid (1,8) starts and stops the sequencer.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Grid (1,8)	Start or stop playback, subject to Shift press stop.
Arm live record

Record notes and edited parameters into the selected channel.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Grid (2,8)	Arm or disarm live recording.
Selecting a Grid Page

Grid (3,8) through (6,8) select the four editors.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Grid (3,8) / (4,8) / (5,8) / (6,8)	Channel / Scale / Pattern / Song.
Tap Pattern again	Cycle Trig, Note and Velocity views.
Norns Menu Navigation

Open tasks with E1; choose a row with E2 and change its value with E3.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
E1 → E2 → K3	Open the context task list, select a task, then open it.
E2 / E3	Select a row / change its value.
K3 / K2 on staged settings	Apply the draft / cancel or return. K3 also confirms a question and K2 cancels it. While an OPEN > row is chosen the last line names the target, for example K3 OPEN RHYTHM, or just K3 OPEN when space is short.
Hold K1 + E3	Change the selected value finely where it supports that.
Hold step + K2 in Masks	Clear all mask attributes of that step.
Tooltips

The screen footer displays controls or feedback for the last grid action.

External MIDI Transport

An external MIDI clock can drive the transport.

MIDI Panic

Send a Note Off sweep without stopping the sequencer.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Hold a non-selected page key (stopping first is optional)	Sweep Note Off across connected MIDI channels; holding the selected page key does not panic.
Quick Control Reference

Use the cheat sheet for a compact list of gestures.

Composition Workflow

Make your first piece. Start with an empty project. Keep it through all ten chapters; you finish with a saved bass-only/full-phrase arrangement.

Assigning Instruments to Channels

Choose one sound. Start with an empty channel and playback stopped. Choose and apply its output before entering notes.

Creating a Rhythm Pattern

Spread the rhythm across a bar. Start with the four-note loop from chapter 3. Move its trigs onto beats 1, 2, 3 and 4.

Applying a Scale

Compare C and D major on the chapter 6 phrase and bass, then restore C major at the end for chapter 8.

Assigning Patterns to Channels

Add a second part. Start with the softer C, C, C, D ending from chapter 5 and an independent second sound. Add a root-and-fifth bass beneath it.

Combining Pattern Overlaps

Trig, note, velocity and length merge choices are independent.

Entering a Melody

Give the phrase an ending. Start with four equal notes on the beats. Raise only the last beat and make it softer.

Adding Parameter Variation

Continue the phrase and bass in C major restored at the end of chapter 7. Add a quiet C pickup before the next bar.

Arranging Song Slots

Arrange two sections. Start with the completed phrase, bass and pickup from chapter 8. Use empty slots 2 and 3; copying overwrites the destination with no undo.

Dig Deeper

Reference sections for pattern editing, channel processing and song arrangement.

Pattern Editor

Edit source-pattern trigs, scale-relative notes and velocities, then assign the patterns to channels.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Grid (5,8)	Open Pattern Trig; press again to cycle Pattern Note and Pattern Velocity.
Pattern Trig: tap grid row 1	Choose one of 16 editable source patterns.
Note and Velocity pages: grid (9,8)–(12,8)	Choose steps 1–16, 17–32, 33–48 or 49–64.
Adding Trigs

Enter pattern trigs manually or preview and paint a generated rhythm.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Pattern Trig: tap row-1 pattern button	Choose the source pattern for editing.
Tap a sequencer step in grid rows 4–7	Toggle a trig; active trigs glow brightly.
Hold a trig and choose its end step	Set the note’s length; dimmer steps show its duration, cut short by another trig in the same pattern.
Tap algorithm button, columns 12–16 of row 2	Select Drum, Tresillo, Euclidean, Numeric Repetitor or Rhythm Doctor.
Tap Paint at grid (16,8), then tap it again	Preview the generated pattern, then commit it; flashing steps show the preview.
Tap Cancel at grid (14,8)	Discard the prepared preview.
Grid (10,8), (11,8), (12,8)	Move the preview left, reset its shift, or move it right; paint to commit.
Grid row 3, columns 12–16, with Drum or Tresillo selected	Select one of five algorithm banks.
Grid row 3, columns 12–15, with Numeric Repetitor selected	Select one of four banks. Euclidean and Rhythm Doctor do not use this bank fader.
Grid row 2, columns 1–10	Set the algorithm’s first parameter. The outer buttons decrement/increment; inner buttons choose broader values.
Grid row 3, columns 1–10	Set the second algorithm parameter for Tresillo, Euclidean or Numeric Repetitor. This fader is disabled for Drum and Rhythm Doctor.
Rhythm Doctor

Select the fifth pattern algorithm at grid column 16, row 2 to capture, analyse and paint rhythm lanes.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
With the sequencer stopped, choose Rhythm Doctor at grid (16,2).	Open capture and paint. Recording, capture setup and Alignment require stopped transport; a finished bank can be browsed and painted while playing.
Empty bank: grid (1,2)	Start Record. Press again or use K3 after ENOUGH / REC OR K3 to finish.
Record before enough audio, or Record on an occupied bank	Open an abandon/clear question; K2 cancels and K3 confirms. Clearing a bank preserves already painted patterns.
Before capture: E2/E3 edit setup → K3 confirm; K2 cancels.	Record uses the confirmed setup. Stereo records both inputs separately; L duplicates the left input and R duplicates the right input into both recorded channels. Manual uses the selected integer BPM from recording start; Auto estimates tempo and phrase start.
Ready bank: select a lane, then E2 field → E3	Browse Window bar/step, sensitivity or paint policy.
In a locally analysed READY bank, press grid (3,2), (4,2) or (5,2).	Select BD (bass drum), SD (snare drum) or CYM (hi-hats and cymbals). The default local detector produces these three lanes; the remote server can declare additional lanes.
Ready bank: select Alignment → K3	Open the tempo, Start beat and fine-start draft. E2 chooses the field; E3 edits. K3 reanalyses the retained recording with the confirmed alignment; K2 cancels. Manual Start beat uses regular confirmed-tempo beats; Auto uses detected beats.
Grid (10,8) / (12,8); hold for a phrase	Move the recording window one step backward / forward, or a whole four-bar phrase.
Grid (11,8)	Return the window to its calculated phrase start.
Select destination pattern in row 1 → grid (16,8) twice	Preview the selected lane, then paint it; grid (14,8) cancels the preview.
If local analysis reports ANALYSIS_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE.	No bank is created. See If local analysis fails for the norns setup needed to retry.
Adding Notes

Set source-pattern notes as scale degrees relative to the channel’s active root.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
From Pattern Trig, press grid (5,8) again	Open Pattern Note.
Tap a note in a step’s grid column	Set a scale-relative note for that source step, including steps without trigs.
Hold K1 while entering a note	Copy the note to the corresponding position on all four sixteen-step pages.
Grid (9,8)–(12,8)	Choose steps 1–16, 17–32, 33–48 or 49–64.
Grid (14,8), (15,8), (16,8)	Move the note range up one scale degree, return to the page with the root on the bottom row, or move it down one scale degree. Hold (14,8) or (16,8) to reach the highest or lowest range.
Hold a row-1 pattern button, or K1 + tap it	Select another source pattern while on the note page.
E3 on Pattern Note screen	View another channel’s resolved steps without changing the selected channel.
Adding Velocity

Set source-pattern velocities using fourteen discrete grid levels from MIDI 127 to 0.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
From Pattern Note, press grid (5,8) again	Open Pattern Velocity.
Tap a level in a step’s grid column	Set that source step’s velocity to the displayed grid level.
Hold K1 while entering a velocity	Copy it to the corresponding position across all four sixteen-step pages.
Grid (9,8)–(12,8)	Choose the sixteen-step page.
Grid (15,8) / (16,8)	Move the displayed velocity range toward higher / lower values; hold to reach an extreme.
Hold a row-1 pattern button, or K1 + tap it	Select another source pattern.
E3 on Pattern Velocity screen	View another channel’s resolved steps without changing the selected channel.
Channel Editor

Select one of 16 channels and open its editing tasks.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Grid (3,8)	Open the Channel Editor.
Tap a channel in grid row 1	Select one of 16 channels; the selected channel supplies the current masks, locks and range.
E1 → E2 task → K3	Open the named channel task; use the task list rather than an old screen-page shortcut.
Grid row 3	Read the currently active scale slot during playback.
Grid (8,8)–(12,8), no step held	Set the selected channel’s octave offset to −2, −1, 0, +1 or +2.
Press grid (10,8)	Set the selected channel’s octave offset to zero.
Devices

Assign an output device to the selected channel.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Channel tasks → Device	Open the output assignment for the selected channel.
E2 Device → E3 → K3	Browse a device and apply the selected output.
E2 MIDI channel or MIDI port → E3 → K3	Choose the route for a MIDI device and confirm it.
MIDI Sound Sources

Route a channel to a configured MIDI output, device and MIDI channel.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Norns MIDI device configuration	Make the required physical or virtual output available to Mosaic.
Channel tasks → Device → E2 field → E3 → K3	Assign the named device or generic CC output, MIDI channel and port.
Norns Sound Sources with n.b.

Select an installed supported n.b. voice for internal audio or Crow output.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Install and enable the supported n.b. mod, then open Channel tasks → Device	Installed supported voices appear in the device picker.
Select the voice with E3 and apply with K3	Route the channel to the chosen internal engine or Crow voice.
Device Parameters

Store MIDI parameter values and transmit them when loading Mosaic or starting playback.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Norns params → the assigned MIDI device parameter	Edit stored patch values; a configured Off value sends nothing.
Load Mosaic or start playback	Transmit the stored enabled MIDI parameters to recall the patch.
Adding Patterns to Channels

Assign one or more source patterns to a channel. A pattern can be used by several channels.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Tap channel in grid row 1	Choose the channel whose source patterns will be changed.
Tap a pattern in grid row 2	Toggle that pattern in the selected channel’s source set; several patterns may be active.
Adding Trig Masks

Add or remove a step trig mask with K1 and the sequencer grid.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Channel Editor: hold K1 and tap a sequencer step	Toggle the step’s trig mask; supply note, velocity and length masks if no source pattern supplies them.
Adding Melodic Notes over Harmony and Drums

Set channel mask defaults or step overrides for note, velocity, length and chord voices.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Channel tasks → Masks → E2 attribute → E3	Set a channel default with no step held.
Hold a sequencer step → E2 attribute → E3	Set an explicit override for that step.
Hold a step and play a MIDI keyboard	Enter note-mask data from the played notes.
Adding Chords

Add up to four chord-mask voices to a root note. The selected output must support polyphony.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Masks → hold step → E2 Chd1–Chd4 → E3	Add up to four scale-relative chord voices to the root; the output must support them.
Assign Chord Strum or Chord Arp in Trig params	Space the chord voices in time rather than playing them simultaneously.
Removing Masks

Clear step-mask overrides without changing channel mask defaults.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Masks: hold step + K2	Clear all step-mask attributes for held steps; channel defaults remain.
Masks: K1 + K2 with no grid key held	Clear all step-mask overrides on the selected channel; preserve channel defaults.
Merge Modes

Set how assigned patterns supply trigs, notes, velocities and note lengths to a channel.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
In Channel Editor, press grid (14,8).	Cycle the shared Strategy through Skip, Only, All, Foundation and Fragments; the sequence wraps.
On Merge modes, select Strategy with E2 and turn E3.	Request the same strategy; the list is clamped and needs no extra K3 Apply.
Press grid (15,8) or (16,8), or hold K1 and press (16,8).	Change note, velocity or length merge respectively when the active strategy permits it. Fragments leaves saved settings unchanged.
Hold note, velocity or length merge button and tap a pattern in row 2.	Choose a source pattern for that attribute when the active strategy permits it.
Trig Merge Modes

Select All, Skip or Only to determine which overlapping pattern trigs play.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Press grid (14,8), or select Strategy on Merge modes and turn E3.	Choose Skip, Only, All, Foundation or Fragments. The grid wraps; E3 stops at each end. Active and Pending

Add or remove a step trig mask with K1 and the sequencer grid.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Channel Editor: hold K1 and tap a sequencer step	Toggle the step’s trig mask; supply note, velocity and length masks if no source pattern supplies them.
Adding Melodic Notes over Harmony and Drums

Set channel mask defaults or step overrides for note, velocity, length and chord voices.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Channel tasks → Masks → E2 attribute → E3	Set a channel default with no step held.
Hold a sequencer step → E2 attribute → E3	Set an explicit override for that step.
Hold a step and play a MIDI keyboard	Enter note-mask data from the played notes.
Adding Chords

Add up to four chord-mask voices to a root note. The selected output must support polyphony.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Masks → hold step → E2 Chd1–Chd4 → E3	Add up to four scale-relative chord voices to the root; the output must support them.
Assign Chord Strum or Chord Arp in Trig params	Space the chord voices in time rather than playing them simultaneously.
Removing Masks

Clear step-mask overrides without changing channel mask defaults.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Masks: hold step + K2	Clear all step-mask attributes for held steps; channel defaults remain.
Masks: K1 + K2 with no grid key held	Clear all step-mask overrides on the selected channel; preserve channel defaults.
Merge Modes

Set how assigned patterns supply trigs, notes, velocities and note lengths to a channel.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
In Channel Editor, press grid (14,8).	Cycle the shared Strategy through Skip, Only, All, Foundation and Fragments; the sequence wraps.
On Merge modes, select Strategy with E2 and turn E3.	Request the same strategy; the list is clamped and needs no extra K3 Apply.
Press grid (15,8) or (16,8), or hold K1 and press (16,8).	Change note, velocity or length merge respectively when the active strategy permits it. Fragments leaves saved settings unchanged.
Hold note, velocity or length merge button and tap a pattern in row 2.	Choose a source pattern for that attribute when the active strategy permits it.
Trig Merge Modes

Select All, Skip or Only to determine which overlapping pattern trigs play.

GESTURE	WHAT HAPPENS
Press grid (14,8), or select Strategy on Merge modes and turn E3.	Choose Skip, Only, All, Foundation or Fragments. The grid wraps; E3 stops at each end. Active and Pending
